tasks.short: Review the referral, history and earlier tests, examine and talk with the patient, decide diagnosis and treatment, and write the visit note.

steps.what: Allergist reviews the referral, history and earlier tests across several screens
Allergist examines and talks with the patient
Allergist diagnoses or treats allergic or immunologic conditions

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.check: A validator flags any allergen, medication, dose or test result not in the record or transcript; the allergist edits and validates before saving.
loop.stop: One draft per visit; if the patient declines recording or the draft is rejected, the allergist writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients describe reactions in their own words; a form does not capture them.

tasks.design: A visit summary in the record ({OTHER}) shows the referral question, known allergies, earlier skin and blood tests and medication together. With consent, a scribe drafts the visit note; a validator flags allergens, medication or results not in the record, and the allergist validates before saving. Examining, diagnosing and treating stay with the allergist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier tests sat in several screens and notes were typed after visits.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribes draft notes the clinician validates; records show visit summaries.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can add reactions the patient did not describe.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a true food allergy from a feared one.
tasks.altitude: The allergist validates drafts instead of typing.

reach.learn: Whether notes and plans are clear.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation and the clinician validates before the note goes into the record.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians reported time per note falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes with Tandem notes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Providers are legally responsible for careful use of generative AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the note written; the letter to the GP is outside.
Input contract: patient consent for recording; fallback is typing.
A DPIA and works council consent come before recording.
research_questions: How often does the validator flag an allergen?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new patients with little history; high: returning patients with many tests.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain diagnosis, prognosis and treatment, show inhaler or auto-injector use, make the allergy action plan, draft replies to follow-up questions, and send them.

steps.what: Allergist educates patients about diagnoses, prognoses and treatments
Allergist shows inhaler or auto-injector use
Allergist writes the allergy action plan by hand
Allergist writes replies to patients' follow-up questions about treatments

loop.input: The patient's question, the record and vetted patient information texts.
loop.output: A draft reply quoting the vetted texts.
loop.check: Every advice sentence must cite a vetted text paragraph or it is dropped; questions about new reactions are not drafted; the allergist edits and approves every reply.
loop.stop: One draft per question; if no sentence passes, the allergist writes the reply.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients ask in their own words; a fixed list of answers does not match them.

steps.what: Allergist sends the reply in the patient portal

tasks.design: The allergy action plan is generated from the record ({OTHER}) with the patient's allergens, symptoms per stage and medication doses, so it is not written by hand. For portal questions, a bounded step drafts replies only from vetted patient texts; questions about new reactions go straight to the allergist, who approves every reply before it is sent. Explaining and showing device use stay with the allergist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Action plans were written by hand and replies written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Records generate plans from structured data; vetted patient texts exist.
tasks.still_hard: Anxious parents ask many personal questions.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a parent feel able to use an auto-injector on their child.
tasks.altitude: The allergist approves replies instead of writing each one.

reach.learn: Whether their action plan is clear.

evidence.claim: Providers are legally responsible for careful use of generative AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from the diagnosis made to the reply sent; treatment changes are outside.
Input contract: vetted texts kept by the clinic; fallback is writing replies.
Patients read portal replies as before.
research_questions: How many drafted replies does the allergist change?

incremental.description: Allergist suggests texts for the vetted library.

approvals.approved_version: The reply as edited and approved by the allergist in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few portal questions; high: many new diagnoses with action plans.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide which tests and allergens, order the tests, perform skin prick tests, read and note wheal sizes, and type results into the record.

steps.what: Allergist decides which diagnostic tests and allergens to use
Allergist orders tests on a paper form
Allergist performs skin prick and intradermal tests
Allergist reads wheal sizes and writes them on a paper grid
Allergist types test results into the record

tasks.design: Tests are ordered from order sets per suspected allergy in the record ({OTHER}), which also print the test layout. Wheal sizes are entered on a tablet grid in the record as they are read, so they are not written on paper and typed in later. Choosing, performing and reading tests stay with the allergist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tests were ordered on paper and results written on a grid and typed in.
tasks.enabler_now: Records hold order sets and tablet result grids.
tasks.still_hard: Delayed patch test readings happen days later.
tasks.human_edge: Judging a borderline wheal against the patient's story.

evidence.claim: Records can hold order sets and tablet grids for test results.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the suspected allergy to results stored; interpretation is outside.
Input contract: order sets and grids set up; fallback is paper.
research_questions: Do transcription errors in test results fall?

incremental.description: Allergist keeps order sets in step with allergen panels.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few tests per patient; high: large panels.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose the medication, check interactions and doses, write the prescription, and explain the medication to the patient.

steps.what: Allergist chooses medication such as antihistamines or glucocorticosteroids
Allergist checks interactions, doses and contraindications
Allergist explains the medication to the patient

tasks.design: Medication surveillance in the prescribing module ({OTHER}) checks interactions, contraindications and doses while the prescription is written, so the allergist does not look them up. Order sets per common diagnosis fill dose and duration. Choosing the medication and explaining it stay with the allergist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Interactions and doses were looked up separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule-based medication surveillance runs in prescribing modules.
tasks.still_hard: Too many alerts get clicked away.
tasks.human_edge: Balancing steroid doses in a child with asthma and eczema.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates; KNMP sets the content.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner; software drafts, it does not prescribe.

assumptions: Boundary: from the diagnosis to the patient instructed; dispensing is outside.
Input contract: prescribing module with surveillance; fallback is looking up.

incremental.description: Allergist reviews and overrides alerts that do not apply.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex patients with many alerts; high: common prescriptions with order sets.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The allergist keeps examining, diagnosing, testing, prescribing and educating patients; screen searching, typed notes, paper grids and look-ups shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An allergist with more time for patients.
